coverageNote: CMMC Level 3: the 24 enhanced security requirements that 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) selects from NIST SP 800-172 (February 2021). What is solid here, stated plainly: (1) Every topicSummary is the VERBATIM requirement text from NIST SP 800-172, extracted from the NIST-hosted PDF; that publication states it "is not subject to copyright in the United States." (2) The SELECTION -- which 24 of 800-172's 35 enhanced requirements CMMC actually adopts -- was read out of 32 CFR Part 170 itself via the eCFR API, not from secondary commentary. All 24 selected identifiers resolved against the extracted 800-172 text with none missing. (3) Every topicLabel is DERIVED from the requirement's opening clause and carries no authority. (4) 32 CFR 170 pairs several Level 3 requirements with organization-defined parameters (ODPs) that the rule specifies. Those ODP values are NOT reproduced here; read the rule's table 1 to 170.14(c)(4) for them before assessing. (5) THIS TIER IS NOT SELF-CONTAINED. Level 3 presupposes Level 2: an organization pursuing Level 3 must also meet all 110 NIST SP 800-171 R2 requirements and hold a Level 2 certification first. Register the level2 tier alongside this one, or the compliance percentage shown will describe 24 requirements while ignoring the 110 underneath them. (6) VERSION TRAP, as with Level 2: NIST withdrew SP 800-172 (Feb 2021) on 13 May 2026 in favour of Revision 3, but 32 CFR 170.2 still incorporates the February 2021 edition by reference. This module tracks the withdrawn edition deliberately, because that is what the regulation binds. Level 3 assessments are conducted by DCMA DIBCAC, not by a C3PAO. Confirm applicability with your contracting officer.

controls.topicSummary: Conduct penetration testing [Assignment: organization-defined frequency], leveraging automated scanning tools and ad hoc tests using subject matter experts.

controls.topicSummary: Use threat indicator information and effective mitigations obtained from [Assignment: organization-defined external organizations] to guide and inform intrusion detection and threat hunting.

controls.topicSummary: Provide awareness training [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] focused on recognizing and responding to threats from social engineering, advanced persistent threat actors, breaches, and suspicious behaviors; update the training [Assignment: organization- defined frequency] or when there are significant changes to the threat.

controls.topicSummary: Include practical exercises in awareness training for [Assignment: organization-defined roles] that are aligned with current threat scenarios and provide feedback to individuals involved in the training and their supervisors.

controls.topicSummary: Employ automated discovery and management tools to maintain an up-to-date, complete, accurate, and readily available inventory of system components.

controls.topicSummary: Identify and authenticate [Assignment: organization-defined systems and system components] before establishing a network connection using bidirectional authentication that is cryptographically based and replay resistant.

controls.topicSummary: Employ automated or manual/procedural mechanisms to prohibit system components from connecting to organizational systems unless the components are known, authenticated, in a properly configured state, or in a trust profile.
